info.name: Oracle HCM - Worker Clone (SELF-CONTAINED)
info.description:
Clone 1-5 workers from Oracle HCM Prod into a lower pod. Basic worker + work relationship + assignment.

Everything is inside this one file. No environment file. No CSV. Works on free Postman.

=====================================================================
STEP 1 - FILL IN THE VARIABLES
=====================================================================
Collection (right-click) > Edit > Variables tab. Fill in:

  prod_host              https://your-prod.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com
  prod_user              read-only Prod service account
  prod_password
  target_host            https://your-test.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com
  target_user            target pod service account
  target_password
  person_number_list     one or more person numbers, comma separated
                         e.g.  100015,100016,100017

Leave rest_version and send_person_number as they are unless told otherwise.

The LDAP job variables are covered in step 2.

>> SECURITY: passwords typed into collection variables are SAVED IN THIS FILE.
>> Do not commit it to source control or email it once filled in. Use the CURRENT
>> value column rather than INITIAL where Postman offers both - CURRENT is not
>> included when the collection is exported.

=====================================================================
STEP 2 - ONE-TIME SETUP PER TARGET POD
=====================================================================
a) Set Person Number generation = Manual in the target pod, so Prod person
   numbers carry across. If that is not possible, set send_person_number = N
   and the pod will assign its own numbers.

b) In the target pod go to Tools > Scheduled Processes and submit
   'Send Pending LDAP Requests' once by hand. Open the process details and copy
   the exact values into these collection variables:
       ldap_job_package
       ldap_job_definition
       ldap_job_parameters
   These differ by release. A wrong value gives an unhelpful 400.

c) Run request 0 once. It checks connectivity to both pods and confirms the
   resource names used by this collection exist in your release.

=====================================================================
STEP 3 - RUNNING IT
=====================================================================
ONE WORKER  - set person_number_list to a single number, then Send requests
              1 through 6 in order.

2 TO 5      - set person_number_list to a comma separated list, then use
              Collection Runner (Run collection). Requests 1-4 and 6 loop
              automatically for each person number. Leave request 5 selected -
              it is skipped inside the loop and submitted once at the end.

Always keep the console open: View > Show Postman Console. Every request logs
what it captured, and request 6 prints a final summary table.

After the run, set passwords from Security Console > search user > Reset Password.

=====================================================================
WHAT GETS CREATED
=====================================================================
  names[]              LastName, FirstName, LegislationCode
  workRelationships[]  LegalEmployerName, WorkerType, PrimaryFlag, StartDate
    assignments[]      ActionCode=HIRE, AssignmentType,
                       AssignmentStatusTypeCode=ACTIVE_PROCESS,
                       PrimaryAssignmentFlag=true, EffectiveStartDate,
                       BusinessUnitId

Not included: job, grade, department, location, manager, phone, address,
national ID. To add one, extend the payload in request 4 and add a lookup
modelled on request 2.

=====================================================================
CAUTIONS
=====================================================================
* Request 3 is NOT optional. POST /workers has no upsert - running request 4
  twice creates two people, and Delete Person is restricted and messy. Keep
  cloned workers in a reserved person-number range so a bad load can be
  identified and end-dated.
* Request 1 is the only Prod call and it is GET-only. Never point requests
  3-6 at Prod. Check target_host before every run.
* Responses contain real names, dates of birth and person numbers. Do not
  export response bodies outside the team.
* Separately worth raising with Oracle via SR: restrict outbound email at the
  pod level in all non-production environments.
* Log every clone: person number, username, pod, date, requester.

=====================================================================
FAILURES
=====================================================================
 401                            wrong credentials
 403                            authenticated but no HCM data role
 req 1 returns 0 rows           person number wrong, or Prod account cannot
                                see that person
 req 2 returns 0 rows           business unit absent in target pod - create it,
                                or set tgt_business_unit_id by hand
 req 2 returns many rows        add ;ClassificationCode=FUN_BUSINESS_UNIT to q
 400 about person number        pod is on automatic numbering - set
                                send_person_number = N
 400 on BusinessUnitId          variable empty or holds a Prod ID - re-run req 2
 404 on hcmOrganizationsLOV     resource name differs in your release - see the
     or userAccounts            describe call in request 0
 req 4 ok but req 6 empty       request 5 has not finished - wait, re-send
 two people created             request 4 was run twice - see cautions

Owner: gr952p

request.description:
Run this once after filling in the variables, and again after any pod refresh.

Checks the target pod is reachable and the service account is authorised, validates the variables you filled in, and resets the worker queue.

CONFIRM RESOURCE NAMES: this collection uses hcmOrganizationsLOV (request 2) and userAccounts (request 6). Both vary by release. To confirm they exist in your instance, send this once by hand:

  GET {{target_host}}/hcmRestApi/resources/{{rest_version}}/describe

The response is large - use Postman's response search box to look for the resource name. If either is absent, find the equivalent name in the describe output and update the URL in the affected request.

Deselect this request when using Collection Runner.

exec: // ---- validate variables and reset the queue ----
function v(k) { var x = pm.collectionVariables.get(k); return (x === undefined || x === null) ? '' : String(x).trim(); }
if (v('prod_host').indexOf('PROD-HOST') > -1)   { problems.push('prod_host is still the placeholder'); }
if (v('target_host').indexOf('TEST-HOST') > -1) { problems.push('target_host is still the placeholder'); }
problems.push('prod_host and target_host are IDENTICAL - this would write to Prod. Fix before continuing.');
console.warn('More than 5 workers queued. This collection is designed for small batches - consider HDL for larger volumes.');
console.log('Confirm that is the pod you intend to write to.');
pm.test('Target pod reachable and authorised', function () {
if (pm.response.code === 403) { console.error('403 - account authenticated but lacks the HCM data role.'); }
console.error('Queue is empty. Set person_number_list before running requests 1-6.');

request.description:
The only Prod call in this collection, and it is GET-only.

The pre-request script picks the next person number off the queue built from person_number_list, so you do not set person_number by hand.

Reads only what the create needs. Captured values are printed to the console.

exec: // ---- pull the current person number off the queue ----
function v(k) { var x = pm.collectionVariables.get(k); return (x === undefined || x === null) ? '' : String(x).trim(); }
// fallback init, in case request 0 was skipped
throw new Error('person_number_list is empty. Fill it in on the collection Variables tab.');
if (isNaN(idx) || idx < 0 || idx >= queue.length) { idx = 0; pm.collectionVariables.set('_idx', '0'); }
// clear anything left over from the previous worker
console.log(' WORKER ' + (idx + 1) + ' of ' + queue.length + '  -  person number ' + queue[idx]);
pm.test('Exactly one worker matched in Prod', function () {
console.error('Person number ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('person_number') + ' returned ' + items.length + ' rows in Prod. Skipping this worker.');
console.warn('  business unit name not returned - set tgt_business_unit_id by hand before request 4.');

request.description:
The only reference lookup a basic hire needs. BusinessUnitId is a pod-specific surrogate key, so it must be resolved here by name - never copied from Prod.

Legal employer goes across by NAME in the payload, so it needs no lookup.

If several rows come back, the first is used and a warning is logged. Narrow it by adding ;ClassificationCode=FUN_BUSINESS_UNIT to the q parameter.

If this 404s, the resource name differs in your release - see the describe call described in request 0.

exec: pm.test('Business unit exists in target pod', function () {
console.warn('  ' + it.length + ' matches - first row used. Confirm it is right, or add a ClassificationCode filter.');
console.error('  business unit "' + pm.collectionVariables.get('src_business_unit_name') + '" does not exist in this pod.');
console.error('  Create it as functional setup, or set tgt_business_unit_id by hand and note the substitution.');

item.name: 3 - Check worker not already in TARGET

request.description:
MANDATORY. POST /workers has no upsert - running request 4 twice creates two people, and Delete Person is restricted and messy.

This must return zero rows before request 4. In Collection Runner, a non-zero result automatically skips the create for this worker and moves on.

exec: pm.test('Worker not already present - safe to create', function () {
console.error('  ALREADY EXISTS in this pod (PersonId ' + it[0].PersonId + '). Create skipped.');

request.description:
Creates worker + work relationship + assignment in one call.

The body is assembled by the pre-request script so empty optional fields are omitted rather than sent as empty strings - Fusion rejects empty strings on ID attributes. The exact payload is printed to the console.

Shape:

{
  "PersonNumber": "100015",
  "DateOfBirth": "1985-04-12",
  "names": [ { "LastName": "...", "FirstName": "...", "LegislationCode": "US" } ],
  "workRelationships": [ {
    "LegalEmployerName": "...",
    "WorkerType": "E",
    "PrimaryFlag": true,
    "StartDate": "2019-06-03",
    "assignments": [ {
      "ActionCode": "HIRE",
      "AssignmentType": "E",
      "AssignmentStatusTypeCode": "ACTIVE_PROCESS",
      "PrimaryAssignmentFlag": true,
      "EffectiveStartDate": "2019-06-03",
      "BusinessUnitId": 300000001234567
    } ]
  } ]
}

Manager is deliberately omitted - the manager often does not exist in the lower pod, and a missing supervisor is the most common create failure. To add a reporting line, clone the manager first, then PATCH the assignment.

exec: // ---- build the payload, omitting empty optional fields ----
function v(k) { var x = pm.collectionVariables.get(k); return (x === undefined || x === null) ? '' : String(x).trim(); }
// safety: never POST to the Prod host
throw new Error('target_host equals prod_host. Refusing to create a worker in Prod.');
throw new Error('Cannot build payload - missing: ' + missing.join(', ') + '. Re-run request 1.');
console.log('  CREATED  PersonId=' + r.PersonId + '  PersonNumber=' + r.PersonNumber);
console.error('  CREATE FAILED - paste the below into the defect or SR:');
// request 5 is submitted once at the end, not per worker

item.name: 5 - Send Pending LDAP Requests (run ONCE at the end)

request.description:
Creating a worker only queues an LDAP request. Until this runs there is no user account and the person cannot sign in. This is the step most often missed - the symptom looks like the create silently failed.

This processes every pending request in the pod, so it runs ONCE after all workers are created, not per worker. The loop handles that automatically.

BEFORE FIRST USE: submit Send Pending LDAP Requests once from Tools > Scheduled Processes, open the process details, and copy the exact Job Package Name, Job Definition Name and parameter string into the collection variables. These differ by release and a wrong value returns an unhelpful 400.

Also run Autoprovision Roles for All Users afterwards if your setup relies on role provisioning rules. Easiest from the UI, or duplicate this request and swap the two job variables.

To poll the status, send this by hand:
  GET {{target_host}}/fscmRestApi/resources/{{rest_version}}/scheduledProcesses/{{ldap_request_id}}
Repeat until the state is SUCCEEDED, ERROR or WARNING. Usually under a minute in a lower pod.

exec: function v(k) { var x = pm.collectionVariables.get(k); return (x === undefined || x === null) ? '' : String(x).trim(); }
throw new Error('ldap_job_package / ldap_job_definition are still placeholders. Submit the process once from Tools > Scheduled Processes, then copy the exact values into the collection variables.');
console.log('LDAP process submitted. Request id = ' + id);
console.log('Poll it, then re-send request 6 for each worker to pick up the usernames.');
console.error('Submit failed. Most likely cause: wrong JobPackageName / JobDefinitionName / ParameterList.');

request.description:
Confirms the user account exists and returns the username.

An empty result immediately after the create is normal - request 5 has not run yet. After request 5 completes, re-send this per worker to collect the usernames.

The test script advances the loop and prints a summary table at the end.

Set passwords from Security Console > search user > Reset Password.

If this 404s, the userAccounts resource name differs in your release - see request 0.

exec: function v(k) { var x = pm.collectionVariables.get(k); return (x === undefined || x === null) ? '' : String(x).trim(); }
console.log('  no user account yet - expected until request 5 has run.');
// ---- record the outcome for this worker ----
postman.setNextRequest('1 - Get worker from PROD (read only)');
console.log(' NEXT: run request 5 once, poll it to SUCCEEDED,');
console.log(' then re-send request 6 per worker to collect usernames.');
console.log(' Then set passwords in Security Console > Reset Password.');
postman.setNextRequest('5 - Send Pending LDAP Requests (run ONCE at the end)');
